name: native-engine-contracts
fault_schedule: test/scenarios/integration/native-engine/case.json; bounded native test transitions; manual WAL flush disables native flush timer for pending durability cases.
assertions: Atomic conditional reads/scans, mutation and outcome writes recover together; aborted writes/deletes do not leak.
Writer-scoped mutation receipts reject foreign handles; admission excludes another transaction until native durability.
Read/replay-only operations use a nonempty native WAL barrier; typed fencing retires the writer permanently.
Caller cancellation and Close cannot destroy pending handles or roll back dispatched commits; manual flush drains and acknowledged data recovers.
A finite delayed stale open can displace a current writer; a fresh current open recovers pre-fence writes and makes progress.
Native suite executes through pinned SlateDB Rust core against pinned MinIO S3 and removes only its scoped resources.
Canceled native Open retains its calling effect through completion and cleanup, preserving cleanup errors.
A staged obsolete writer attempts an actual user commit after takeover; native fencing rejects it and the mutation is absent after reopening.
Four production adapter source mutations must each fail their named invariant: stale commit success, premature durable read, omitted replay result and close while in use.
Parent-owned scoped Compose identity permits bounded fallback cleanup if the native child exits or is killed.
limitations: MinIO S3-emulator evidence is not AWS qualification.
No production controller/service cutover, registry authority validation, arbitrary OS scheduling, process-kill schedule, or scale claim.
Native/Rust/OS timing is real; deterministic driver clock qualification is separate.
